directAnswer: Phishing emails often contain suspicious links, poor grammar, and requests for personal information. Always verify the sender's email address and look for unusual requests.
summary: Recognizing phishing emails is crucial for protecting your personal information and avoiding scams. This guide provides steps to identify common signs of phishing attempts.

sections.heading: Common Signs of Phishing Emails
sections.body: Phishing emails may include generic greetings, urgent language, and requests for sensitive information. Look for misspellings and inconsistencies in the sender's address.

sections.heading: How to Verify the Sender
sections.body: Check the sender's email address carefully. Phishing emails often use addresses that mimic legitimate ones but may have slight variations, such as extra characters or different domains.

sections.heading: Checking Links Safely
sections.body: Hover over links without clicking to see the actual URL. Ensure it matches the expected website and is secure (https://).

steps.title: Examine the Email Address
steps.detail: Look closely at the sender's email address for any discrepancies or unusual domains.

steps.title: Look for Urgency and Threats
steps.detail: Be cautious of emails that create a sense of urgency or threaten account suspension if immediate action isn't taken.

steps.title: Check for Grammar and Spelling Errors
steps.detail: Many phishing emails contain poor grammar or spelling mistakes, which can be a red flag.

steps.title: Verify Links Before Clicking
steps.detail: Hover over links to preview the URL before clicking. Ensure it directs to a legitimate site.

faqs.question: What should I do if I suspect an email is phishing?
faqs.answer: Do not click any links or provide any information. Report the email to your email provider and delete it.

faqs.question: Can phishing emails come from legitimate-looking addresses?
faqs.answer: Yes, attackers can spoof email addresses to make them appear legitimate. Always verify the sender's address.

faqs.question: What are some examples of phishing tactics?
faqs.answer: Common tactics include fake invoices, account verification requests, and messages claiming to be from tech support.

caveats: Phishing tactics evolve constantly, so always stay updated on the latest scams.
